Gas lines installed, tested and signed off.

Licensed gas line installation, leak testing, and appliance hookups. Every job ends with a pressure test, so you know the line holds before we leave.

Call (844) 212-9186

If you smell gas

  1. 1Leave the building and take everyone with you.
  2. 2Don't flip switches, light flames or run anything electrical.
  3. 3From outside, call your gas utility or 911.

Once it's safe, call us for the repair and a full leak test.

Pick an appliance to see what a hookup includes

Range and cooktop

A gas branch to the kitchen with a shut-off valve you can reach and a connector sized to your range.

  • Shut-off valve within reach
  • Connector matched to the range
  • Leak test at every joint
  • Burner and ignition check

How we test for leaks

A line isn't finished until it's proven tight. We use more than one method, because each one catches something the others can miss.

  • Pressure test

    We pressurize the line with a gauge attached. If the needle holds over time, the line is tight.

  • Electronic gas detector

    A sensitive handheld detector pinpoints leaks at fittings, valves and connectors.

  • Soap solution

    Bubbling at a joint shows exactly where gas is escaping, so the fix goes in the right place.

What your gas line is made of

MaterialWhere it's usedGood to know
Black iron pipeMain lines and most interior runsRigid and long-lasting, with threaded joints.
CSST (flexible stainless tubing)Retrofits and hard-to-reach runsQuicker to route through walls. Needs proper bonding.
Appliance connectorsFinal link to the applianceReplaced when an appliance is moved or reinstalled.

Material choice follows local code and your system. We confirm it before quoting.

Signs of a gas leak

  • A rotten-egg smell near an appliance or the meter
  • A hissing or whistling sound near a gas line
  • A pilot light or burner flame that burns yellow or orange
  • Dead plants in a strip over a buried line

Adding an appliance or moving a line?

Tell us what you're connecting. Most gas work needs a permit and an inspection, and we'll explain what your city requires before we start.
